gloss.def.ndvi: Satellite greenness index: high values = more active vegetation, low = bare or dry soil.
gloss.def.et: Water the soil and plant return to the air; it signals crop water demand.
gloss.def.anomaly: Difference from what is normal for that time of year, measured against previous years.
gloss.def.waterBalance: Available rain minus what the crop needs in its cycle; negative = deficit.
gloss.def.gdd: Useful heat (above 10 °C) a crop accumulates to complete its cycle.
gloss.def.et0: Reference evapotranspiration (mm/day): what a well-watered lawn would evaporate; the base for estimating how much water a crop needs.
gloss.def.soilAnomaly: Difference between the soil moisture the satellite sees and what is normal for this time of year (%); negative = drier than usual.
gloss.def.frost: Day with a minimum temperature of 0 °C or less. On the calendar, the fraction of the month's days meeting that condition.
gloss.def.frostFree: Stretch of the year without likely frosts (days): between the last spring frost and the first autumn one.
gloss.def.satGround: A satellite pixel averages several km² and does not know your plot's exact elevation; that is why it can differ from a station inside the field.
gloss.def.bareSoil: Months with no living crop or cover (low NDVI); the soil is left exposed to erosion.
gloss.def.enso: ONI index of the Pacific phase: El Niño usually brings more rain to the Pampas; La Niña, less.
gloss.def.hydroGroup: Soil hydrologic group (A–D): how fast water infiltrates; A infiltrates a lot, D tends to pond.
